title: Cloud restore bypasses the safe database restore lifecycle
body:
<!-- omera-review-2026-10-05:R01 -->

## Summary and actual behavior

**Reproduced and code-confirmed.** [cloud_backup.rs:903](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src-tauri/src/cloud_backup.rs#L903) makes a raw rollback copy of only the live main database, ignores backup errors, and copies the restored file directly over the active database. [commands.rs:4739](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src-tauri/src/commands.rs#L4739) calls this while `AppState` and workers still hold database connections; restart occurs only afterward. The database enables a 256 MB mmap at [db.rs:177](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/crates/omera-storage/src/db.rs#L177).

With a synthetic active WAL connection, this Windows build fails with `Failed to replace live database ... user-mapped section open (os error 1224)`. No real database was restored. On systems allowing the copy, the source path still has active connections/WAL and non-atomic replacement risk; corruption or WAL contamination was not demonstrated on this host. Local restore already uses `recovery::stage_restore`, so cloud restore should use the same lifecycle.

## Environment and evidence

- Baseline: Omera 0.4.3, `dev` at [`bdac8fb`](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/commit/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5); SQLite schema 15.
- Review host: Windows; the inspected application was launched from the repository root with `pnpm run tauri dev`.
- Evidence strength is stated above. For code-confirmed scenarios, the steps below describe a targeted validation scenario rather than a completed end-to-end reproduction. Remote-provider, destructive real-library and cross-platform scenarios were not exercised.

## Reproduction or validation scenario

1. Create a temporary SQLite database using `Database::connect`, leaving its WAL-enabled connection open.
2. Create a different snapshot using `create_cloud_snapshot` with the LocalPath provider.
3. Call `restore_cloud_snapshot` for the active path while the first connection is alive.

## Expected behavior

Restore is staged and activated before opening SQLite connections; the current database remains recoverable on failure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Use the existing staged restore lifecycle and activate before connections/workers start.
- [ ] Validate integrity, schema and foreign keys; create a consistent, verified rollback snapshot.
- [ ] Test active WAL, Windows mmap, interrupted activation, failed rollback creation and restart recovery.

## Related work and scope

Related closed issues: #98. This report describes the remaining behavior on the baseline above and does not assume that every earlier fix is absent.

Implementation must respect the lead-owned persistence, file-safety, migration or update-trust boundaries in [ENGINEERING_HANDOFF.md](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/docs/ENGINEERING_HANDOFF.md). Use synthetic fixtures and preserve source data. Any implementation PR should target `dev`.

## Standalone production-function reproduction

Create `docs/reviews/repro-2026-10-05/Cargo.toml` with the manifest below and `src/lib.rs` with the test source below. Run from the repository root:

```powershell
cargo test --manifest-path docs/reviews/repro-2026-10-05/Cargo.toml --target-dir target probes:: -- --test-threads=1
```

```rust
mod cloud_backup;

#[cfg(test)]

    use omera_domain::*;
    use omera_storage::Database;
    use std::{fs, path::Path};

        let writer = fs::File::create(path).unwrap();
        let mut encoder = png::Encoder::new(writer, 64, 32);

        encoder.set_depth(png::BitDepth::Eight);
        encoder.add_text_chunk("parameters".into(), "confidential prompt\nNegative prompt: private negative\nSteps: 20, Sampler: Euler, CFG scale: 7, Seed: 123, Size: 64x32, Model: private-model".into()).unwrap();
        encoder.write_header().unwrap().write_image_data(&vec![120; 64 * 32 * 3]).unwrap();
    }

    fn make_file(path: &Path, folder_id: i64) -> ImageFile {
        ImageFile {
            id: None, folder_id, path: path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
            size_bytes: fs::metadata(path).unwrap().len(), modified_at: 1,
            container: Container::Png, metadata: omera_metadata::extract_metadata(Container::Png, path),

            stack_id: None, stack_order: 0,
        }
    }

            sidecar: ExportSidecar::TextPrompt, filename_template: "{name}".into(),
            destination_path: "unused".into(), as_zip: false, max_edge: None,
            export_html_showcase: false, html_title: None,
        }
    }


    #[test]
    fn cloud_restore_must_survive_active_wal_connection() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let active_path = dir.path().join("active.db");
        let active = Database::connect(&active_path).unwrap();
        active.add_folder("active-before-checkpoint").unwrap();
        active.connection().execute_batch("PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE);").unwrap();
        active.add_folder("active-in-wal").unwrap();
        let snapshot_db = Database::connect_in_memory().unwrap();
        snapshot_db.add_folder("restored-snapshot").unwrap();
        let cloud = dir.path().join("cloud");
        let config = CloudBackupConfig { local_path: Some(cloud.to_string_lossy().into_owned()), ..Default::default() };
        let created = crate::cloud_backup::create_cloud_snapshot(&snapshot_db, &config, dir.path(), None).unwrap();
        let filename = created.snapshot.unwrap().filename;
        let restored = crate::cloud_backup::restore_cloud_snapshot(&active_path, &config, &filename).unwrap();
        assert!(restored.success);
        drop(active);
        let reopened = Database::connect(&active_path).unwrap();
        let folders = reopened.list_folders().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(folders.len(), 1, "Cloud restore reported success, but active WAL overwrote the restored data: {folders:?}");
        assert_eq!(folders[0].path, "restored-snapshot");
    }
}

```

title: Deferred pipeline cleanup does not revalidate the destination or source identity
body:
<!-- omera-review-2026-10-05:R03 -->

## Summary and actual behavior

**Code-confirmed.** [commands.rs:4331](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src-tauri/src/commands.rs#L4331) trashes the queued source pathname once its deadline arrives. It does not use `target_file_id` to check that the managed copy still exists and matches, or verify that the source pathname still represents the file originally ingested. Cleanup is invoked during application startup.

If the destination disappears before the grace period ends, cleanup can remove the remaining original. If a generator replaces the source with a new file at the same path, cleanup can remove that newer file instead.

## Environment and evidence

- Baseline: Omera 0.4.3, `dev` at [`bdac8fb`](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/commit/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5); SQLite schema 15.

## Reproduction or validation scenario

1. In an isolated pipeline fixture, harvest an item with delayed source cleanup enabled.
2. Before the cleanup deadline, remove the managed destination; alternatively replace the source at the same pathname.
3. Run `process_pipeline_cleanups` and inspect the original/new source and cleanup receipt.

## Expected behavior

Cleanup preserves a source unless the verified managed destination exists and the source still matches the ingested item.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Record and revalidate source identity and destination content immediately before cleanup.
- [ ] Use `target_file_id` and a durable receipt; retain a deferred/failed state when validation fails.
- [ ] Test destination loss, replaced source, trash failure and restart; exclude external vaults and unrelated media.

title: Legacy configuration migration records success after persistence failure
body:

## Summary

**Code-confirmed.** Migration ignores credential-migration and destination-save errors, then appends a successful config artifact. An absent destination has revision zero; saving a legacy config with a nonzero revision can be rejected by the normal optimistic-concurrency check. title: Add a main-toolbar toggle for sensitive-content masking
body:
<!-- omera-review-2026-10-05:R37 -->

## Problem

The global sensitive-content masking preference is available inside Settings, but the main gallery has no readily accessible control for changing it. Users switching between private viewing, a shared workspace and screen sharing must interrupt browsing and navigate through the settings dialog.

The user raised this usability concern during the native application review. Source inspection confirms the preference is exposed in SettingsModal and passed from App.vue into VirtualGrid, while the gallery toolbar provides sorting, zoom and view-mode controls without a masking toggle.

## Environment and evidence

Omera 0.4.3, Windows development application on dev. Reviewed runtime baseline: [bdac8fb](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/commit/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5); subsequent merge a4ac24f changes issue templates/contribution documentation only.

- [Settings preference](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src/components/SettingsModal.vue#L844)
- [Gallery toolbar](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src/App.vue#L2356)
- [Current runtime masking state](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src/App.vue#L313)
- [Per-image reveal state](https://github.com/BerryUIKI/Omera/blob/bdac8fbcdbac5535075e091453b77c3afe518ba5/src/components/VirtualGrid.vue#L85)

## Proposed interaction

Add a one-click toggle at a stable location in the main gallery toolbar, near the view-mode controls. Show both an icon and explicit localized state, such as **Masking on** / **Content visible**. The control should remain available without selecting an image and at normal/narrow window sizes.

Recommended preference model: Settings retains the startup default; the quick control changes the current viewing session. The interface should distinguish the active session state from the saved startup default.

Enabling masking should immediately conceal sensitive items again, including images temporarily revealed earlier in that session. Disabling masking should visibly indicate that content is exposed. This is a presentation control; it does not change an image's NSFW classification or the library's metadata.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Provide a discoverable, one-click toolbar control with clear current-state text.
- [ ] Apply the change immediately using the shared presentation state without rescanning, reclassifying or changing source files.
- [ ] Clear temporary reveal overrides when the user explicitly enables global masking.
- [ ] Make the control keyboard-operable, expose its toggle state to assistive technology, and provide a documented shortcut that respects focused inputs and modal dialogs.
- [ ] Localize all control text and keep the action available at narrow widths and without a selection.
- [ ] Make session/startup-default behavior explicit and test navigation, view changes and previously revealed items.

## Scope and dependencies

This issue covers quick access and feedback for the masking control. Existing Table-mode enforcement is tracked in #252, and classification false positives in #296. Those reports remain separate; the toolbar control must not imply that unresolved presentation surfaces are protected.

Implementation PRs target dev. Follow the repository's presentation, virtualization and configuration compatibility rules. This is a UX proposal; no implementation is included in this report.
